newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland police fear girl's killing sectarian.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland police fear girl's killing sectarian.

text.p: Northern Ireland police said on Wednesday that the shooting of an 18-year-old Roman Catholic girl at the home of her Protestant boyfriend may have been sectarian.
"We are working on the premise that the motive may have been sectarian," a spokesman for the Royal Ulster Constabulary said.
A maverick Protestant extremist group, the Loyalist Volunteer Force (LVF), denied involvement in the girl's murder in a telephone call to a Belfast news organisation.
The LVF, which says it is fighting to stop Northern Ireland being reunited with the overwhelmingly Catholic Irish republic, said in a statement that such acts "were not on its agenda."
Eighteen-year-old Bernadette Martin was shot in the head by a gunman who slipped into the home of her boyfriend at Aghalee, some 30 miles (50 km) southwest of Belfast on Tuesday.
One man was arrested for questioning on Tuesday and police said they had detained a second on Wednesday. No further details were available.
Confirmation of a possible sectarian motive raised fears among community leaders of possible reprisals and cast further doubt about a ceasefire which Loyalists called in October 1994.

Police have blamed Loyalists, so-called because of their allegiance to Britain, for a series of recent attacks including attempted bombings of the offices of Sinn Fein, political wing of IRA guerrillas fighting British rule of the province.
The LVF is a breakaway group which does not recognise the truce called by mainstream Loyalist organisations.
It was the first death since a week of violent Catholic opposition erupted to Protestants' Orange Order parades through Catholic areas.
A suspected Loyalist activist was killed in Belfast last week when a home-made bomb he was handling exploded.
